paragraphs.text: File the plumbing scope as a subsequent filing under the existing job number, rather than as a new unrelated job, if it is part of the same construction project. DOB guidance says all filings for the same project should share the job number; a subsequent filing adds new scope and work types and may use a new applicant. It is separately processed and may have a different review type from the initial filing. The initial filing must be submitted—not remain in pre-filing status—before the subsequent filing can be initiated and submitted; it may be submitted before the initial filing is permitted and until an LOC is issued for the initial filing.

For completion, the general guidance says an LOC is requested separately for each initial and subsequent filing. However, if the existing job is an NB or Alteration-CO filing, the specialized FAQ says no LOC is requested for its subsequent filing: that filing remains Permit Entire, while only the I1 changes to CO issued. The supplied guidance does not resolve whether the subsequent record may be created before I1 is submitted; it says the fields will not update until I1 is submitted and recommends completing as much of I1 as possible before creating it.

paragraphs.text: The appropriate DOB NOW action is a Post Approval Amendment (PAA): it is the stated route for changes after a filing has been approved, and the Applicant of Record must file it using the same Applicant of Record as the original filing. Because this filing was not submitted for legalization, the stated legalization bar does not apply. Only one PAA may be in progress, and Department review and approval are required; a PAA cannot be used to request sign-off.

Disclose the revised scope in the Plans/Work (PW1) Comments field. Revised plans call for a complete plan set: include new unapproved sheets and previously approved, DOB-stamped sheets; following approval, the uploaded new set replaces the prior plan set. The filing review type, application/location address, Applicant of Record information, owner information, and building type are not editable. The supplied guidance is unresolved on Work on Floors: the process page lists it as non-editable, while the FAQ specifically says a PAA can add or remove a floor and requires PW3 to reflect the resulting increase or decrease in estimated work cost. Cost changes can also recalculate fees.

evidenceLimitations: The supplied official guidance gives incompatible directions on whether Work on Floors is editable in a PAA; it does not resolve how that field should be handled for this revision.
